app.title: EnvGeo Seawater — exploring seawater isotope and hydrographic data
app.summary: A person picks a bundled reference collection and can add their own measurement table as an overlay. They narrow the records with shared filters for time, location, depth and measured values. Then they look at the subset in several linked views: property–property scatter plots with an optional regression line, sampling-location maps, temperature–salinity diagrams and depth profiles. Selecting points in a scatter plot finds them on a map. A separate utility screens pairs of datasets for records that may be repeats of the same observation. The person leaves with figures, filtered tables, summary statistics and audit tables of overlap candidates.

task.text: Filter a combined collection of seawater sample records, compare their isotope and hydrographic properties across plots and maps against reference data, and export figures and audited subsets.

data.text: Tables of seawater samples from several cited reference collections plus an optional table uploaded by the user. Each row has a position, depth, date, stable water isotopes, salinity and temperature, plus its source citation and quality flags.
data.item: one seawater sample at a station, depth and date, with its isotope and hydrographic measurements

stage.text: exploring and comparing compiled seawater measurements against reference datasets, including checking newly collected samples

mechanism.text: Shared sidebar filters feed every page, and each page draws the filtered subset as a different kind of plot. Uploaded rows are drawn on top. In the 2D view, box or lasso selection on a scatter plot narrows the map below it to the chosen samples. The overlap utility runs a pairwise screen with editable tolerances and lists Strong and Review candidates for inspection and export.

field.text: stable water isotope and hydrographic analysis (δ18O–salinity relationships, T–S diagrams, depth profiles) in marine geochemistry and oceanography

workflow.name: filter a combined record collection and compare it across linked plots and maps, then export figures and subsets

steps.here: Choose one of three bundled reference collections with a radio button. A CSV/XLSX upload is optional: its columns are standardised and its numbers cleaned of stray spaces, and it is kept only for the session.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Sidebar range sliders for year, longitude, latitude, depth, salinity, δ18O and temperature, plus month, cruise/transect, dataset and reference/citation choices. The same filters also apply to the uploaded overlay.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Plot d18O–salinity, dD–d18O, T–S or any two parameters, coloured by a third, with an optional least-squares regression line and its statistics. T–S diagrams carry approximate σ0 density contours. d-excess is derived from the isotopes.
Box or lasso a group of points on the scatter plot. The sampling map below re-centres on just those samples, and a separate table lists the selected rows.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Map one chosen parameter as a scatter or contour map, with region presets, a choice of map centre, colour-range sliders and an offline coastline style.

steps.step: find possible repeated records across sources
steps.here: Choose a dataset pair, adjust the Strong and Review tolerances for latitude, longitude, depth, salinity and δ18O, and run the screen. Then inspect each candidate's source rows side by side and optionally note a decision for this session.
Download self-contained interactive HTML figures, static map images, the filtered or selected rows as CSV, a filtered-data summary CSV of conditions and statistics, and the candidate audit CSVs.

distinctive: Each record carries its source citation, and data can be filtered by reference, so every figure keeps its provenance.
Uploaded measurements are drawn in front of the reference data for comparison, but they stay in memory for the session and are never merged into the bundled workbooks.

Overlap screening only compares records with the same year and month and sorts candidates into two disjoint classes, Strong and Review. It never deletes source rows; any hiding of candidates can be undone.
Built to work offline aboard a research vessel: there is a local coastline fallback, and HTML figures embed Plotly so they still work without a network.
Domain plots: T–S diagrams with approximate σ0 contours, d18O–salinity regression, and depth profiles that break the line at gaps.
